action: Phoenix Tours customers: be wary of emails or LINE messages about an "order error" or "duplicate order", and use the company line or the 165 anti-fraud hotline to check.
date_note: The company says it found the attack on 16 November; the date of its announcement is not given in the article, published 20 November.
exec: A Taiwanese travel firm says some customer order data may have been accessed; customers face impersonation scams.
geo_basis: country; the article does not state the company's city
plain: Taiwanese travel company Phoenix Tours says hackers attacked its systems and some customers' names, phones, emails, addresses and itineraries may have been accessed.
summary: According to a company announcement relayed by CTWANT, Phoenix Tours found on 16 November that its system had been attacked by hackers. Some order data was suspected of unauthorised access, and may include names, phone numbers, emails, addresses and itineraries. The company says no card, passport or ID numbers have been found accessed so far, and it has told the authority and police. The number affected is not stated.
title: Phoenix Tours says hackers attacked its systems; some customer order data may be exposed

validation.note: Read the CTWANT article quoting the company announcement; the announcement itself was not opened and no second publisher was found.

review.note: Compared title, 16 Nov find date, data list, no card/passport/ID found, authority and police notified, no count against CTWANT article quoting company announcement
